name: MX25L3233FM2I-08G
title: MX25L3233F: 32 Mbit 3 V serial NOR flash with single, dual and quad I/O, 133 MHz
summary: A 32 Mbit (4,194,304 x 8) serial NOR flash running from 2.65 V to 3.6 V. It talks SPI in mode 0 or 3 and can move address and data over two or four I/O lines, reading at up to 133 MHz, with execute-in-place and 8/16/32/64-byte wrapped bursts. The array erases in 4 KB sectors, 32 KB or 64 KB blocks, or whole, and programs in pages of up to 256 bytes; it adds a 4 Kbit one-time-programmable area, block protection, program/erase suspend and SFDP. MX25L3233FM2I-08G is the 200 mil 8-pin SOP, industrial temperature range.

operation.text: The array is 4,194,304 bytes, seen as 33,554,432 x 1 bit on single I/O, 16,777,216 x 2 in dual mode and 8,388,608 x 4 in quad mode. It holds 1024 sectors of 4 KB, 128 blocks of 32 KB and 64 blocks of 64 KB, each erasable on its own. With one I/O the bus is SCLK, SI and SO with CS# selecting the chip; in quad mode SI, SO, WP# and HOLD# become SIO0 to SIO3. Addresses are 3 bytes; every command code is one byte.
Mode 0 (CPOL 0, CPHA 0) and mode 3 (CPOL 1, CPHA 1) both work. Input bits are taken on the rising SCLK edge and output bits change on the falling edge.

Read-type commands (2READ, 4READ, DREAD, FAST_READ, QREAD, RDCR, RDID, RDSCUR, RDSFDP, RDSR, READ, REMS, RES) may be ended by raising CS# after any output bit. Write-type commands (4PP, BE, BE32K, CE, ENSO, EXSO, NOP, PP, Resume, RST, RSTEN, SE, Suspend, WRDI, WREN, WRSCUR, WRSR) run only if CS# rises exactly on a byte boundary; otherwise they are dropped. An unknown command sends the device to standby until the next CS# falling edge, with SO high impedance. Array accesses during a write-status, program or erase cycle are ignored and do not disturb it. Check status before issuing a command.

With CS# low, pulling HOLD# low pauses communication without deselecting: the pause starts on the HOLD# falling edge if SCLK is low, or at the next SCLK low otherwise, and ends the same way on the rising edge. While held, SO floats and SI is ignored. An internal write-status, program or erase keeps running. Raising CS# during a hold resets the interface logic; to restart, HOLD# goes high and CS# low. Hold is unavailable in quad mode (QE = 1).
WP#/SIO2 and HOLD#/SIO3 have internal pull-ups while the pin is left unconnected; the pull-up is turned off once the pin is wired in the system.

PP, 4PP, SE, BE, BE32K, CE, WRSR and WRSCUR need WREN first to set WEL. WEL clears at power-up and on completion of WRDI, WRSR, PP, 4PP, SE, BE32K, BE, CE, suspend, software reset and WRSCUR. A program or erase aimed at a protected area does nothing but still clears WEL. Read WIP until it is 0 before checking WEL.

BP3 to BP0 (non-volatile, default 0) choose how many 64 KB blocks are read-only, from 1 up to all 64, counted from the top of the array when TB = 0 or from the bottom when TB = 1. TB is a one-time-programmable bit in the configuration register, written with WRSR, default 0. Chip erase runs only with all BP bits at 0.

With SRWD = 1 and WP# low the device is in hardware protected mode: WRSR is refused and SRWD, BP3 to BP0 and TB are fixed until WP# is driven high. If WP# is tied permanently high only the software (BP/TB) protection is available. Setting QE disables hardware protection. When SRWD = 1, WP# must meet tWHSL before and tSHWL after a WRSR.

QE (status bit 6, non-volatile, factory 0) must be 1 for QREAD, 4READ and 4PP; with QE = 0 these are ignored and pins 3 and 7 act as WP# and HOLD#. With QE = 1 they are SIO2 and SIO3 and the hold and hardware-protection functions are off.
WRSR (01h), after WREN, takes a status byte then a configuration byte and starts a self-timed cycle tW when CS# rises; WIP is 1 for its duration, after which WEL clears. It cannot change WIP or WEL.
ODS (configuration bit 0, volatile, written with WRSR) selects full output drive or one quarter drive.

READ (03h) runs to 50 MHz with no dummy byte. FAST_READ (0Bh) adds 8 dummy clocks for 133 MHz. DREAD (3Bh) and QREAD (6Bh) take the address on SI and return data on two or four lines after 8 dummy clocks. 2READ (BBh) and 4READ (EBh) also send the address on two or four lines; their dummy count follows DC: 2READ 4 clocks to 104 MHz or 8 to 133 MHz, 4READ 6 to 104 MHz or 10 to 133 MHz. Every read starts at any byte, auto-increments, rolls over from the top address to 0, and continues until CS# rises. Reads are rejected while a program, erase or WRSR is running.

In 4READ the two clocks after the address carry P[7:0]. If each upper nibble bit differs from its lower partner (for example A5h, 5Ah, F0h, 0Fh), the device stays in read after CS# rises and the next access starts directly with the address, saving the 8 command clocks. A value without toggling (for example FFh, 00h, AAh, 55h) ends the mode on the next CS# rise. Resume is ignored while this mode is active.

SBL (C0h or 77h) followed by a wrap code turns on wrapped reads of 8, 16, 32 or 64 bytes, aligned to that boundary around the start address; code 1xh turns it off. It is off after power-up or reset and stays as set until then. 4READ (EBh) uses the wrap.

PP (02h) or 4PP (38h, QE = 1, address and data on four lines) programs 1 to 256 bytes within one 256-byte page after WREN; bits only go from 1 to 0, so the target bytes must be erased first. Bytes past the end of a page wrap to its start, and if more than 256 bytes are sent only the last 256 are kept. CS# rises after a whole byte to start the self-timed tPP cycle; WIP reads 1 until it ends.

SE (20h), BE32K (52h) and BE (D8h) erase the 4 KB sector, 32 KB block or 64 KB block holding the address; CE (60h or C7h) erases everything. Each needs WREN, must end with CS# on a byte boundary, and runs self-timed (tSE, tBE32K, tBE, tCE) with WIP set. Erased bits read 1. A protected target is left unchanged and WEL is cleared.

Issue WREN, confirm WEL = 1 with RDSR (and check BP3 to BP0), send the program or erase, then poll RDSR until WIP = 0. Check the result either by reading back the data or by reading P_FAIL and E_FAIL in the security register.

Suspend (75h or B0h) pauses PP, SE, BE32K or BE. After tPSL or tESL (20 µs max) WEL is 0 and PSB or ESB is 1; the array then reads normally except for whichever page, sector or block was being written. During an erase suspend a page program is allowed outside the suspended area (after WREN); that program runs to completion, with no suspend of its own, before the erase may resume. RDSR, RDSCUR, RDCR, WRDI, RES, RSTEN, RST and NOP may be sent at once after suspend. Resume (7Ah or 30h) sets WEL and WIP back to 1 and clears PSB or ESB; wait tPRS or tERS before suspending again, and at least the typical time for the operation to progress.

DP (B9h) drops the supply current from ISB1 to ISB2 tDP after CS# rises. Only RDP/RES (ABh) is accepted then; power cycling or reset also wakes it. After RDP, CS# stays high for tRES1 before the device is in standby; after RES (which also reads the old 1-byte ID 15h), tRES2.

RDID (9Fh) returns C2h, 20h, 16h. REMS (90h) with two dummy bytes and an address byte of 00h returns C2h then 15h; with 01h the order is reversed, and the pair repeats while CS# stays low. RES returns 15h and is kept for older designs; RDID is the one to use.

A separate 4 Kbit area (addresses xxx000h to xxx1FFh) holds a unique identifier. ENSO (B1h) enters it, normal read and program commands then act on it, and EXSO (C1h) leaves; the main array is not reachable meanwhile, and WRSR, WRSCUR, CE, BE, SE and BE32K are refused. Security bit 0 shows a factory lock; WRSCUR (2Fh, after WREN) sets LDSO (bit 1) to lock the customer part permanently, after which only reads work.

RSTEN (66h) then RST (99h) returns the device to standby with all volatile bits at their power-on defaults; any other command between them cancels the reset. A reset during program or erase can corrupt that data. Recovery takes tRCR after a read, tRCP after a program and tRCE after an erase.
RDSFDP (5Ah) with a 3-byte address and 8 dummy clocks returns the JESD216 parameter tables, which describe the read modes, erase sizes, voltage range and features.

The device powers up in standby with WEL cleared, guarded by a power-on reset. CS# must not select the device until VCC has reached its minimum and tVSL has passed, and must follow VCC down at power-down; a pull-up on CS# helps. Writes are inhibited below VWI. For a clean restart VCC must fall below VPWD for at least tPWD. A capacitor of about 0.1 µF next to the package pins decouples VCC.
Shipped erased (every byte FFh) with the status register at 00h.
The USON, WSON and XSON packages have an exposed pad underneath. It may float or join the GND pin's ground, and connects to nothing else; keep vias and traces from under it.
